c.tagline: Peru's 'White City', carved from volcanic sillar beneath the cone of El Misti.

taxi.fareNote: Most Arequipa taxis are unmetered, so agree the fare before getting in (short in-town rides run about S/6-10). Uber, InDrive and Cabify all operate and give an upfront price, though driver numbers are lower than in Lima.

emergency.note: 105 reaches the national police; 116/106 is for medical/ambulance (SAMU). Arequipa sits at about 2,335 m, so altitude is gentler than Cusco, but still ascend slowly and hydrate.

avoid.reason: Express-kidnapping via unofficial taxis; caution in the centre at night

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed colonial core built from white sillar volcanic stone, wrapped around the Plaza de Armas, cathedral and Santa Catalina Monastery; best for first-timers who want every major sight, restaurant and bar within walking distance.

Arequipa's oldest quarter, a maze of narrow whitewashed alleys, tiny plazas and viewpoints just north of the centre; photogenic and atmospheric, quieter at night, and popular with travelers who want charm a short walk from the action.

A leafy, upscale residential district across the Chili River, famous for its arched sillar mirador framing El Misti and its traditional picantería restaurants; suits those wanting calm streets, sunsets and classic volcano views.

A quiet, green pocket just south of the centre with mid-range and larger hotels along shaded avenues; good for families and travelers who want to be near the historic core without the crowds and noise.

A modern district on the northern heights with malls, cafes and a scenic plaza and mirador; practical for longer stays, remote work and those wanting contemporary comforts a short taxi ride from the old town.
lodging: Katari Hotel at Plaza de Armas

water.note: Drink bottled or purified water; tap water is not reliably safe for visitors.

transit.pay: Pay the flat fare in cash to the driver or fare collector on board - about S/1 (~$0.30) for a city combi ride. There is no rechargeable transit card; carry small coins.
transit.hours: Combis and micros run roughly 5am to 10-11pm; after that, taxis (agree the fare first) fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Arequipa has no metro or tram; the compact sillar-white colonial centre is best explored on foot, with combis and taxis covering longer trips and the outer districts of Yanahuara, Cayma and Cerro Colorado.

bus: Combis & colectivos to Yanahuara, Cayma & the outskirts

transit.m: Combi/colectivo from the main road outside the terminal to the center, ~30-40 min
Taxi to Plaza de Armas, 15-25 min

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving ~10% at sit-down restaurants for good service is appreciated.

places.name: Sol de Mayo

food.name: Ocopa arequipena

places.name: La Capitana

places.name: Sol de Mayo

places.name: La Benita de los Claustros

places.name: Mercado San Camilo

places.name: Sol de Mayo

places.name: Chicha por Gaston Acurio

food.desc: Despite the name no cheese: a churned frozen custard of milk, coconut and cinnamon, scraped into cups by street vendors and dusted with cinnamon.

places.name: Mercado San Camilo

places.name: La Nueva Palomino

places.name: La Capitana

landmarks: Monasterio de Santa Catalina
A 16th-century citadel-convent painted in vivid blues and oranges, its silent lanes and cloisters forming a city-within-a-city for cloistered nuns.
Plaza de Armas and Basilica Cathedral
Peru's most graceful main square, framed by white sillar arcades and a cathedral stretching the full plaza width beneath El Misti volcano.
Iglesia de la Compania
A Jesuit church whose intricately carved 1698 sillar facade epitomises Andean baroque, hiding a gilded altar and the jewel-like San Ignacio chapel.
Museo Santuarios Andinos
Home of 'Juanita the Ice Maiden', the frozen Inca girl sacrificed atop Ampato volcano 500 years ago and discovered remarkably preserved in 1995.
Mirador de Yanahuara
A whitewashed viewpoint of sillar arches inscribed with poetry, perfectly framing El Misti's snowcap above the White City's rooftops.
Monasterio de la Recoleta
A 1648 Franciscan monastery across the Chili River, its four cloisters holding a wondrous antique library and Amazon ethnographic collections.
Mercado San Camilo
A cast-iron market hall attributed to Gustave Eiffel's workshop, overflowing with queso helado, hundred-variety potatoes, and fresh juice stalls.
Mansion del Fundador
The restored colonial estate of Arequipa's founder Garci Manuel de Carbajal, its vaulted sillar rooms furnished with viceregal art beside the Socabaya River.
Molino de Sabandia
A picturesque 1621 stone watermill still grinding grain in a countryside oasis of ponds and pastures beneath volcano views.
Ruta del Sillar (Sillar Quarries)
The dazzling white canyon quarries of Anashuayco, where carvers still hand-cut the volcanic sillar stone that built and named the White City.

train.note: Peru has no international passenger trains. PeruRail's Belmond Andean Explorer luxury sleeper runs between Arequipa, Puno and Cusco on set departures - a two-night hotel-on-rails rather than transport, and priced accordingly. There is no ordinary scheduled train from Arequipa, so almost everyone travels by coach.

intl.to: La Paz (Bolivia) - via Puno and Desaguadero

bus.note: Long-distance coaches use the Terrapuerto and Terminal Terrestre south of the centre, where a small terminal fee is payable. Cruz del Sur, Oltursa (https://www.oltursa.pe/) and Civa run to Lima in about 16 hours, Cusco in 10 and Puno in 6. For Chile you normally change in Tacna and cross to Arica by colectivo; for Bolivia the Hop buses handle the border formalities for you.

ferry.note: Arequipa is inland at 2,300 m beneath El Misti with no navigable water, so there are no ferries. The nearest passenger boats are the Lake Titicaca launches from Puno, about six hours away, out to the Uros floating islands and Taquile.

half.name: Sabandía & Yanahuara
half.blurb: The colonial Sabandía water mill and the arched Yanahuara mirador make an easy half-day of countryside, sillar architecture and El Misti views on the city's edge.

full.name: Colca Canyon & the Cruz del Cóndor
full.blurb: One of the world's deepest canyons, three hours north, where Andean condors ride the morning thermals at the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint amid terraced Colca Valley villages and hot springs.

full.name: Salinas y Aguada Blanca National Reserve
full.blurb: A high-altitude reserve on the Colca road with grazing vicuñas, flamingo-dotted salt lagoons and volcanic altiplano beneath Misti, Chachani and Pichu Pichu.

full.name: Toro Muerto Petroglyphs
full.blurb: Thousands of pre-Columbian rock carvings scattered across a desert field in the Majes Valley, one of the largest petroglyph sites in the world.
